title: G-Drive wins Estoril and steals the LMP2 title from TDS
dek: Harry Tincknell, Giedo van der Garde and Simon Dolan won the 4 Hours of Estoril by 51 seconds in the G-Drive Gibson, taking the LMP2 title as the leading Thiriet by TDS Oreca stalled in the garage.

chapters.title: A title decided at the last, in Portugal's final ELMS round
text: The 4 Hours of Estoril on 23 October 2016 closed the six-round European Le Mans Series season with the LMP2 crown still open. Thiriet by TDS Racing's Oreca #46 arrived 14 points clear of the G-Drive Racing Gibson #38, 92 to 78, with Mathias Beche and Pierre Thiriet leading Simon Dolan, Harry Tincknell and Giedo van der Garde in the drivers' standings. The SMP Racing BR01 #32 of Andreas Wirth and Stefano Coletti was 24 points off the top and needed a win and a collapse from both rivals. There was a prize beyond the trophy as well: the winner of the LMP2 title was guaranteed a place on the grid for the 2017 Le Mans 24 Hours.

The field was thinner than at Spa. Thirty-seven cars were entered and 36 reached the grid, with ten in LMP2. Algarve Pro Racing had sent its cars off to open the Asian Le Mans Series in Zhuhai, Team WRT had treated its Spa appearance as a one-off, and Murphy Prototypes' Oreca was too badly damaged from the Spa accident to be rebuilt in time. Eurasia Motorsport reshuffled its crew for the finale: Pu Junjin and Nico Pieter de Bruijn left for what the team called business reasons, and Michael Lyons and Frédéric Vervisch joined Tristan Gommendy in the Oreca #33. Pegasus Racing's team manager Julien Schell replaced Remy Striebig in the Morgan.

The weekend carried plenty of farewells. It was the last ELMS race at Estoril, with the round moving to Portimão for 2017, and the final outing for the Jota-run Gibson 015S. Practice set an uneasy tone: Beche topped a foggy first session in 1:31.637 before a heavy crash for the Ultimate LMP3 car ended it under a red flag, and Saturday morning's second session was run on a wet track that dried late, with Nicolas Lapierre fastest in the DragonSpeed Oreca on 1:35.671 and van der Garde second.

chapters.title: Lapierre takes pole on a drying track
text: Qualifying was a gamble on conditions. The track stayed wet for much of the session, and DragonSpeed chose intermediates for the Oreca #21 on the strength of the Michelin runners' pace in such conditions. Early on Dimitri Enjalbert and then Paul Loup Chatin led the way, Chatin reaching 1:45.455 for the Panis Barthez Ligier before Olivier Pla's Dunlop-shod Krohn Ligier moved ahead on 1:45.237 as the flag fell. The surface kept improving through the final laps, and Lapierre, who had lifted on his penultimate lap to clear his run, crossed the line on 1:44.146, his third pole of the season.

Chatin held second on 1:44.553, about four tenths back, and Giedo van der Garde was a late third in the G-Drive Gibson on 1:44.758. Pla was fourth and Vitaly Petrov fifth for SMP on 1:45.857, with Enjalbert sixth. The championship leaders were in trouble: Thiriet by TDS lined up seventh, roughly three seconds off the pole after Beche had an early moment, while Eurasia started 20th overall at the back of the LMP2 runners after a difficult session and a Saturday crash for Vervisch in practice. Race day was set for a 13:30 local start.

chapters.title: Van der Garde jumps the pole car
text: The start belonged to van der Garde. From the second row he went around the outside of the grid and took the lead through the first corner, running wide, but Lapierre soon took it back. Chaos behind: Fabien Barthez spun into the barriers at turn 3 from the front row, and a lap later Patrice Lafargue did the same in the IDEC Ligier #28 at the same place, both cars rejoining at the back. Gommendy's Eurasia Oreca came through the field from the rear and picked up some damage in contact.

Eight minutes in Lapierre had a gap of nearly four seconds, but the Gibson reeled him in and by lap ten the pair were nose to tail. Van der Garde's attempt to pass the leading GTE Ferrari, the AF Corse #51, at turn 6 brought contact and a black-and-white warning for both cars, with no penalty. Just before the first stops van der Garde retook the lead on lap 31. He pitted a lap later with Dolan taking over, and DragonSpeed's decision to double-stint its tyres kept Henrik Hedman ahead out of the pits. Hedman then ran through the gravel at turn 3, and Dolan passed him around the outside at turn 4 to lead as the hour ended. Hedman's afternoon had only begun to go wrong, with a big lock-up and more contact that dropped the Oreca to fourth.

chapters.title: The leaders fall apart
text: Dolan eased away from Pla's co-driver Niclas Jönsson, who in turn pulled clear of Thiriet. Wirth and Julien Canal's Greaves Ligier were a distant fourth and fifth. The Thiriet by TDS car only had to finish fifth or better to take the title, and for a while all looked well.

It unravelled at the second routine stop. Ryo Hirakawa climbed aboard the Oreca #46 and the car would not fire up. It was pushed on to the dollies and into the garage with an electrical fault, and a place on the podium became a tumble down the order. Beche, clearly dejected, confirmed the electrical problem. By halfway Dolan led by nearly 40 seconds from the Krohn Ligier, and the title was slipping away from the French team.

chapters.title: Safety car, and a crippled rival
text: The only Safety Car of the race came early in the third hour, after the championship-leading JMW Ferrari, limping with a cracked gearbox casing, was hit at turn 2 by the spinning United LMP3 Ligier of Mike Guasch. Both cars made it back to the pits, but the JMW was retired. The field bunched up, and Dolan, right on the button for the restart, let the lapped DragonSpeed car through and set about rebuilding his advantage. Canal pulled the Greaves Ligier off with a retirement.

At the next stops Dolan handed the Gibson to Tincknell for the run to the flag. Krohn's long stop put Pla back in third behind Coletti, and with 80 minutes left Tincknell led SMP by 43 seconds. Pla caught the BR01 in traffic before the end of the hour and, after some side-by-side contact, got ahead. Thiriet's car returned to the track with about 90 minutes remaining after 44 minutes in the garage, far too late to matter.

chapters.title: Fresh tyres, a long gap
text: With 40 minutes left Pla made his last stop from second, more than a minute behind the leader. Tincknell followed two minutes later for fuel only and emerged with the lead intact, and when the stops were done he held a 70-second margin over Coletti, with Pla pressing the SMP car and Lapierre coming up fast behind both. Fresh rubber made the DragonSpeed driver's pass look easy: by the 26-minute mark he was through into third and soon after went by the BR01 for second.
Behind, Lyons had worked the Eurasia Oreca up to fifth, laps down after its earlier issues. The fight for the final podium place was on between Pla and Coletti, nose to tail for a quarter of an hour.

chapters.title: Rain arrives as Tincknell wins
text: Rain fell for the final 20 minutes, adding drama to the battle for third. With five minutes to go both Coletti and Pla lost grip at the rear; Pla spun and rejoined about six seconds behind, and the Krohn Ligier finished fourth, just over eight seconds from the BR01. Tincknell, on an untroubled run, took the flag after 145 laps and 4:01:32 to win by 51.157 seconds from Lapierre, Hanley and Hedman in the DragonSpeed Oreca, a car that Hedman's early errors had taken out of the fight for victory. Coletti, Wirth and Petrov brought the SMP BR01 home third.

Gommendy, Lyons and Vervisch took the Eurasia car to fifth, two laps down, with IDEC sixth four laps behind. The fastest lap of the race, 1:32.898, went to Lapierre. Panis Barthez finished seventh in class, and the stricken Thiriet by TDS car was classified 28th overall, 24 laps behind. Pegasus's Morgan, which had taken the flag ninth overall, was later excluded.

chapters.title: G-Drive takes the title, TDS falls short
text: The result handed the LMP2 championship to G-Drive Racing, the Jota-run team, and to Dolan, Tincknell and van der Garde, who came into the weekend 14 points down. Tincknell said the team had won it by being the most consistent through the season. Van der Garde, a rookie in endurance racing after a year without a drive, said it was not bad for a first season, while Dolan said the team's behind-the-scenes work had made the difference and that the Gibson 015S could now be retired as one of the most successful chassis in LMP2 history.

For Thiriet by TDS it was another painful finale. A team that had led the standings into the last race finished without the title after electrical trouble that cost it more than 20 laps. Lapierre said DragonSpeed's aggressive tyre choices had not been best for Hedman and that his final set of new tyres allowed him to climb to second. Wirth complained of traffic from slower LMP3 cars, and Pegasus Racing's Morgan, originally ninth overall, was excluded from the results.
G-Drive, as LMP2 champion, earned an automatic invitation to the 2017 Le Mans 24 Hours, one of four awarded through the ELMS.

The next season will look different. The 2017 entry list was due to be revealed on 2 February, and the LMP2 class expects to grow: RLR MSport announced a Ligier JS P217 programme, Villorba Corse confirmed Andrea Belicchi alongside Giorgio Sernagiotto and Roberto Lacorte in a new Dallara, and the Oreca 07 was about to begin testing. The series returns to Portugal at Portimão in 2017.

facts.v: Nicolas Lapierre put the DragonSpeed Oreca on pole with 1:44.146 on a drying track, about four tenths ahead of Chatin's Panis Barthez Ligier.

facts.t: First ELMS title for G-Drive and Jota
facts.v: Tincknell won by 51.157 seconds from DragonSpeed in the last outing for the Gibson 015S, claiming the first ELMS championship for G-Drive Racing and Jota.

facts.t: Late rain for the podium fight
facts.v: Rain fell in the last 20 minutes and Pla spun while chasing Coletti for third, leaving the SMP BR01 on the podium.
